page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the arm64 architecture. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by the Neoverse-N3 CPU model, with 2 physical cores and 1 thread per core. The server is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes a cache hierarchy consisting of 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 112 MB L3 cache. It supports AES cryptography instructions, but does not include local storage or bundled public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a mixture of performance characteristics. Single-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng is average at 2058.78, while multi-core performance is weak at 4086.82. Single-threaded gzip compression performance is strong at 32.69 GB/sec, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression is average at 9.4 GB/sec. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is poor at 18.69 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show poor performance for small-block read-only cached operations at 141.61 GB/sec and weak performance for large-block read-only uncached operations at 36.91 GB/sec, though large-block write operations achieve an average rating of 36.72 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput is weak at 5.09 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n4a-standard-2 offers an entry-level dedicated arm64 resource profile with a balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The lack of bundled local storage and public IPv4 addresses, combined with weak multi-core and memory bandwidth results, indicates a tradeoff favoring lower-intensity workloads over resource-heavy applications. This server is suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, single-threaded processing tasks like basic compression, and low-traffic web serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4a-standard-2 is an arm64-based general-purpose server featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs on the Neoverse-N3 processor and 8.0 GB of RAM. The CPU configuration includes 2 physical cores, 1 thread per core, and a 112 MB L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. It does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-threaded gzip compression at 32.69 GB/sec and average single-core stress-ng performance. However, multi-core CPU performance and memory read bandwidth are weak to poor. With a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server represents an entry-level dedicated arm64 option. It is suited for lightweight general-purpose applications, single-threaded utility tasks, and low-volume web serving where high multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth are not critical.
